history.rationale: reproducing test FAILS on buggy and PASSES on fixed; numerical probes are disabled (--no-probes), so the test transition is the whole of the evidence

plans.objective: Reconstruct E_B and E_F so the developer test yields a valid F2P: make one selected datetime64 DateOffset case fail on /workspace/buggy and pass on /workspace/fixed without changing T_dev.
assumptions: The bundled developer test T_dev is sensitive to pandas correctness for DateOffset-iNaT handling and finer-resolution promotion overflow/wrapping.
A build/runtime environment choice (Python/Numpy/Cython) can determine whether the buggy code path is exercised enough for the test to genuinely fail (vs pass).
Choosing a specific Python version and pinning NumPy to a known compatible minor can make the bug manifest consistently.

actions.step: Check current venv Python versions for buggy and fixed to decide if a rebuild on a specific CPython is needed.
Build both revisions with a controlled toolchain and NumPy version expected to reproduce the DateOffset arithmetic bug reliably.
Run only the selected developer test case with -k on the buggy revision; confirm it fails with an assertion/test failure (not collection/import).
Run the same selected developer test case on the fixed revision; confirm it passes.

plans.success_criterion: For the chosen -k case in pandas/tests/arithmetic/test_datetime64.py, T_dev (1) fails on buggy revision with a real test assertion/failure, and (2) passes on fixed revision.
